classification.difficultyReason: Halve the given base before applying Pythagoras’ theorem to find the perpendicular height.

content.prompt:
An isosceles triangle $ABC$ has equal sides $AB=AC=14\text{ cm}$. The side $BC$ is $26\text{ cm}$. A line $AD$ is drawn at right angles from $A$ to $BC$. This divides $BC$ into two intervals of equal length. Find the length of $AD$, correct to 2 decimal places.

Use the square-root table on printed page 206 (source PDF page 12) to work out the square root you need.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 5 diagram, bottom of printed page 209
spec.description: Isosceles triangle with apex A, base endpoints B and C, and foot D. Equal base intervals have single ticks. AD is dashed red and perpendicular to BC. Ordinary source-blue outlines are rendered black in house style.
spec.mathematics: AB=AC=14 cm; BC=26 cm is given in the stem; BD=DC; AD is perpendicular to BC.
spec.answerVisibility: Only original givens and marks are visible; neither the half-base length nor the altitude answer is printed.

answer.worked:
The base is divided into equal intervals, so $BD=26\div2=13\text{ cm}$.

By Pythagoras’ theorem in right-angled triangle $ABD$:
$$\begin{align*}AD^2+13^2&=14^2\\AD^2+169&=196\\AD^2&=196-169\\AD^2&=27\\AD&=\sqrt{27}\\AD&\approx5.20\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
The square-root table gives $\sqrt{27}\approx5.20$, correct to 2 decimal places.
